title: How does it work?
intro: Bio-Dosha-12 is a body-balance monitor that combines the constitution theory of traditional medicine with modern calculation methods.

s1.title: 1. Find your constitution
s1.body: Answer 12 simple questions once to set your inborn body type (constitution) and your base number, Kt. The “How can I tell?” button on each question shows, with an animation, a practical way to check your answer.

s2.title: 2. Measure for 30 seconds a day
s2.body: Just enter your weight — the season is applied automatically and your BEDI balance index appears straight away.

s3.title: 3. Follow your remedies
s3.body: Food and lifestyle remedies that match your deviation are suggested automatically. Age-specific needs (children, older adults) are taken into account as well.

q1.q: How do I answer the questions correctly?
q1.a: Press the “How can I tell?” button under each question to see an animation of a practical way to check that trait. For example, bone size is found with the wrist test: grasp one wrist with the other hand — if the thumb and index finger overlap, your bones are small; if the tips just touch, medium; if they don't touch, large. The animation cycles through the three outcomes, and tapping an answer freezes it on that state.

q2.q: How often should I take the assessment?
q2.a: Just once. Your constitution is inborn, so it does not change. Instead, enter your weight every day or every week to track your balance. If you think you answered wrongly, you can retake the assessment at any time.

q3.a: It means your current weight is within the balance range for your age, sex, height, constitution and the season. The closer your deviation is to 0, the better your balance. This is an assessment of body balance, not a full health check.

q4.q: Why are my results different in winter and summer?
q4.a: Each season affects the body differently: winter adds heaviness towards Badgan (Earth), and summer adds lightness towards Khii (Wind). This is a natural fluctuation, so the calculation accounts for it automatically.

q5.q: How do I track my family members?
q5.a: Add a member in the “Family” section and take the assessment for them. Then enter each member's weight separately to track them.

q6.a: Following traditional medicine guidance, honey is not given to children under 13 — the system filters it out automatically and gives only age-appropriate recommendations. Talk to a doctor before changing a child's diet.

q7.q: How do the practitioner pages (Patients, Reports) open?
q7.a: Patient records open through a medical organization. Ask your clinic's owner or manager for an invitation, or register your own organization. Once the organization is verified and you have turned on 2-step sign-in, Patients and Reports appear in the menu. An organization's managers run its members and settings but do not see patient records.

organizations.a: When you create an account, choose the organization type and enter your clinic's details. If you already have an account, you can register the organization from the Organization page. A new organization first shows as “Waiting for verification”; meanwhile you can complete its profile and invite colleagues. Patient records open after platform staff have checked and verified it. Every member of an organization uses 2-step sign-in.

invitations.a: The organization's owner or a manager creates an invitation on the Organization page with the colleague's email and role (practitioner, manager or owner). The invitation link is shown only once and expires after a while. The invited person opens the link and either creates an account or signs in with the invited email to accept. Only owners can make someone an owner.

mfa.a: Besides your password, you sign in with a 6-digit code from a phone app that changes every 30 seconds. It is required for platform staff and every member of a medical organization, and optional for individuals. You can use Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 2FAS, Authy or a similar app. During setup, 10 recovery codes are shown only once — print them or keep them somewhere safe. If you are running low, create new ones in Settings on the Security tab.

mfaLost.q: What if I lost or changed my phone?
mfaLost.a: At sign-in, enter one of your recovery codes (format XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) instead of the app code — each code works once. Individuals can then turn 2-step sign-in off in Settings on the Security tab and set it up again on the new phone. Organization members and platform staff, and anyone without recovery codes left, should tell their organization's owner or manager and contact the system administrator. After confirming who you are, the administrator resets 2-step sign-in and you set it up again on the new phone.

plans.a: A personal account comes with a free plan that holds a set number of profiles (yours and your family members'); a family plan holds more. A medical organization's plan sets the number of practitioners and patients and whether PDF reports are included. When you reach a limit, the app tells you at that moment. For now plans are assigned by the system administrator, so contact them to upgrade.

methodology.title: Research basis
methodology.body: The BEDI method was validated by a study of 400 medical records carried out in 2023–2025 at the Tumurbaatar Otoch traditional medicine clinic. The statistical deviation thresholds, calculated from the relationship of age, height and weight (based on the standard deviation), matched the practitioner's actual diagnosis exactly in 81% of cases, a statistically highly significant relationship (p < 0.01).
methodology.citation: V. Tumurbaatar, “Determining individual body variation from the relationship of age, height and weight”, Tumurbaatar Otoch clinic.

disclaimer: This system does not replace a doctor's examination or diagnosis. Consult a qualified practitioner before following any recommendation. If a serious health problem appears, seek medical care.
contact: Read more about the method on the <link>About</link> page. For account or sign-in problems, contact your organization's owner or manager, or the system administrator.
